cards.text: Meet Zephaniah, a prophet in the days of Josiah, king of Judah (Zephaniah 1:1). He just finished warning that the LORD will stretch out His hand against Judah and all who dwell in Jerusalem (Zephaniah 1:4). Now he calls out, “Gather yourselves, gather together, O shameful nation,” and then he gives a reason to hurry.

cards.question: Zephaniah tells the shameful nation to gather together. What does he want them to gather before?

answers.text: The Day of the LORD's anger

cards.text: Three times in one verse he says “before”: before the decree takes effect, before the burning anger of the LORD, before the Day of the LORD's anger. Friend, that's not a gentle reminder, that's an oven timer going BEEP BEEP BEEP.
Then the prophet turns to all the humble of the earth, the ones who carry out His justice.

cards.question: What does Zephaniah tell all the humble of the earth to do?
Zephaniah promises the humble they will surely be sheltered on the day of the LORD's anger.

cards.text: He tells them to seek righteousness and seek humility, and says, “Perhaps you will be sheltered on the day of the LORD’s anger.” Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer hoping somebody would come looking for tape, so when I hear a perhaps like that, I lean ALL the way in.
Then Zephaniah starts naming cities, four of them: Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod and Ekron.

cards.question: Gaza will be ___, and Ashkelon left in ruins.

cards.text: Ashdod will be driven out at noon, and Ekron will be uprooted. NOON, friend, no sneaking out at midnight, they'll get driven out in broad daylight.
Then comes a “Woe” for the dwellers of the seacoast, the nation of the Cherethites, and the word of the LORD is against Canaan.

cards.question: The word of the LORD is against Canaan on the seacoast. Whose land is it?

cards.text: Then the LORD says, “I will destroy you, and no one will be left.” So what will happen to a coastline with nobody on it?

cards.question: The emptied seacoast will become a land of pastures, with wells for shepherds and folds for sheep.
Zephaniah says the coast will end up belonging to someone. Who?
Zephaniah says the ones who take the coast will lie down in the evening among the houses of Ashkelon.
Zephaniah says the LORD their God will attend to them and ___ their captives.

cards.text: Now the LORD speaks about Moab and the Ammonites, two nations descended from Lot (Genesis 19:36-38). He says, “I have heard the reproach of Moab and the insults of the Ammonites,” and then He says what they did.

cards.question: Moab and the Ammonites taunted the LORD's people and threatened their ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, describes what's coming for them: “a place of weeds and salt pits, a perpetual wasteland.” Perpetual, friend, that's not a fixer-upper, that's a FOR SALE sign NOBODY ever takes down.

cards.question: The LORD says Moab will be like one famous city and the Ammonites like another. Which pair of cities?
The LORD says the remnant of His people will plunder Moab and the Ammonites.
Moab and the Ammonites get all this in return for their ___, for taunting and mocking the people of the LORD of Hosts.

cards.text: The LORD will be terrifying to them when He starves all the gods of the earth. Every one of those gods will find out what the back of a junk drawer feels like, and trust me, I've got the dust to prove it.

cards.question: Zephaniah says the nations of every shore will do something, each in its own place. What?

cards.text: Next comes one short line for the Cushites, a people from Cush, south of Egypt: “You too, O Cushites, will be slain by My sword.” Then the LORD will stretch out His hand against the north.

cards.question: The LORD stretches out His hand against the north. Which nation will He destroy?

cards.text: Nineveh is named too. Yes, THAT Nineveh, the great city Jonah tried so hard not to visit (Jonah 1:2-3).

cards.question: The LORD will make Nineveh a desolation, as dry as a desert.
Once Nineveh is a dry desolation, who moves in?

cards.text: Owls will roost atop her pillars, and their calls will sound from the window. That's not a city, friend, that's a nature documentary where the narrator is whispering.
Desolation will lie on the threshold, for He will expose the beams of cedar. Nobody's answering that door.
Then Zephaniah calls Nineveh “This carefree city that dwells securely…” She's like the friend who leaves the oven on, walks out the door and says, “Relax, it's FINE.”

cards.question: What does Nineveh, the carefree city, think to herself?

answers.text: That no one else compares to her

cards.question: People passing by ruined Nineveh stop to weep for her.

cards.text: Zephaniah says the city that thinks to herself, “I am it…” will be a ruin, a resting place for beasts, and everyone who passes by her hisses and shakes his fist. Friend, that's every cookie that ever bragged it couldn't burn.
